summary: H.R. 8981, known as the SCALE Biology Act, establishes a biometrology laboratory program within the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). The program focuses on measurement research, technical standards, and data reliability for engineering biology, biomanufacturing, and biotechnology. It authorizes specific funding appropriations from fiscal year 2026 through 2030, mandates reports and implementation plans for Congress, and updates related definitions and authorities.

affected_groups.effect: May access user facilities with advanced equipment and participate in developing technical standards, roadmaps, and collaborative partnerships.
affected_groups.group: Industry and businesses involved in engineering biology, biomanufacturing, and biotechnology

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to engage in collaborative partnerships, consortia, extramural research support, and graduate and postgraduate research training.
affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education and nonprofit organizations

affected_groups.effect: Required to coordinate with NIST on research, development, risk management, and technical standards.

key_provisions: Establishes a biometrology laboratory program at NIST for measurement research in engineering biology, biomanufacturing, and biotechnology.
Directs NIST to perform research supporting voluntary, consensus-based technical standards, guidelines, best practices, and methodologies.
Authorizes funding appropriations for the NIST program ranging from $55,000,000 for fiscal year 2026 to $85,000,000 for fiscal year 2030.
Requires the Director of NIST to support engineering biology foundries, graduate and postgraduate research and training, and public lexicons of definitions.
Mandates interagency coordination with Federal departments, the Manufacturing USA Program, and the Department of Energy regarding biomass feedstock utilization.
Requires an implementation plan to be submitted within the first fiscal year and a comprehensive program report to be submitted within three years.
missing_information: The exact allocation details across specific internal NIST labs beyond general program authorizations are not detailed.
Long-term economic outcomes or specific regulatory enforcement mechanisms outside of standards and security controls are not mentioned.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 8981, known as the SCALE Biology Act, establishes a biometrology laboratory program within the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). The program focuses on measurement research, technical standards, and data reliability for engineering biology, biomanufacturing, and biotechnology. It authorizes specific funding appropriations from fiscal year 2026 through 2030, mandates reports and implementation plans for Congress, and updates related definitions and authorities.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a formalized federal measurement program for engineering biology and biomanufacturing within NIST, backed by multi-year funding authorizations spanning fiscal years 2026 through 2030. It sets structured requirements for interagency coordination, standard-setting, research foundries, and congressional reporting.
